This message comes from Angie. Angie has been helping homeowners find skilled pros
to get their home projects done well for over 30 years. For everything from minor repairs
to major remodels, find reviews, pricing, and booking at Angie.com or on the Angie app.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Ryland Barton. Microsoft is pushing back against
accusations of visa fraud from the Trump administration. The federal government
suspended the company from a program that allowed it to apply for green cards on behalf
of employees in the country on H-1B visas. For member station KUOW, Monica Nicholsberg reports.
Vice President J.D. Vance accused Microsoft of abusing the H-1B system more than any other company.
Microsoft laid off last year 6,000, 6,000 American workers. At the same time,
the company benefited from 6,300 H-1B visas and almost 3,000 green cards.
In a statement, Microsoft said the vast majority of those applications were to renew the status
of employees already in the country. They were not, in other words, new hires intended to replace
laid-off workers. Microsoft also said it only hires foreign employees who meet the rigorous
standards of the visa category. For NPR News, I'm Monica Nicholsberg in Seattle.
Hurricane Isaias has strengthened into a Category 2 storm with a maximum sustained
wind of 100 miles an hour. Tristan Wood with member station WFSU reports it's headed for the
North Gulf Coast and is projected to make landfall between tomorrow night and Saturday morning.
Isaias is currently projected to make landfall somewhere between Panama City,
Florida and Mobile, Alabama. Florida Governor Ron DeSantis says seven Florida counties have
already begun evacuations in low-lying areas along the coast. This storm has the potential
to produce. I think right now they're in the range of five to seven feet of storm surge.
That's significant storm surge. Forecasters warn that Isaias could strengthen into a major
Category 3 hurricane as it turns over the unusually warm waters of the Gulf. But they
are also watching a wall of strong atmospheric wind shear, which they hope will act as a break,
disrupting the storm's core and preventing it from becoming that strong before making landfall.
For NPR News, I'm Tristan Wood in Tallahassee. The Justice Department has filed a new indictment
against former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and his wife. The couple now face a torture charge
in addition to drug trafficking and gun counts, NPR's Ryan Lucas reports. Nicolas Maduro and his
wife Celia Flores Maduro have been in U.S. custody since they were captured in an American military
raid in January. The Medeiros were charged with narco-terrorism, drug and weapons offenses for
allegedly working with drug cartels to traffic cocaine to the United States. They have pleaded
not guilty. Now they are facing one additional charge of torture. Prosecutors allege Maduro
used violence, including torture, to maintain power in Venezuela. The alleged abuse included
electric shock, rape, starvation and threats to kill victims' families. Prosecutors say U.S.
citizens were among those subjected to such measures. The couple is scheduled to go on trial
in June. Ryan Lucas, NPR News, Washington. Mortgage rates marched higher for the seventh
week in a row. You're listening to NPR News from Washington. Lawyers for Christa Pike say she has
taken her first steps with assistance one week after a failed execution in Tennessee left her
in critical condition. She was sentenced to death for a 1995 murder. The lethal injection drug didn't
kill her and her lawyer said her arms were left bruised and blistered. It was Tennessee's second
failed execution in four months. Florida held a hearing today on ending rules that require four
vaccines in schools and daycares. Carrie Sheridan of member station WUSF reports. The idea is to make
some shots optional. They include chickenpox, hepatitis B, pneumococcal disease and homophilus
influenza type B, a bacteria that can cause meningitis. Florida Surgeon General Joseph
Latipos spoke at the hearing. I believe and the department's position is that parental rights
are extremely important and parental rights they absolutely need to be protected. Florida already
allows religious exemptions to vaccines. Some members of the public asked why changing the
rules is a good idea medically. Latipos said it's not about the science. We're not making a comment
about the importance or the lack of importance of any vaccines. If the rules change it could happen
later this month. For NPR News, I'm Carrie Sheridan in Tampa. Major League Baseball is proposing to
shorten the regular season to 154 games from 162 games starting in 2029. Cutting games would reduce
the opportunity for players to set records. Baseball's five-year labor contract expires
December 1st and management is expected to lock out players. This is NPR News.
